<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<asp>

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Grid dimensions
N = #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
M = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.

row(R) :- R >= 0, R < N.
col(C) :- C >= 0, C < M.

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Manhattan distance
ManhattanDist(R1,C1,R2,C2,Man) :- Man = abs(R1 - R2) + abs(C1 - C2).

% Distance to nearest 2 and 3
dist2(R,C,D2) :- D2 = #min{R0,C0 : input(R0,C0,2), abs(R - R0) + abs(C - C0)}.
dist3(R,C,D3) :- D3 = #min{R0,C0 : input(R0,C0,3), abs(R - R0) + abs(C - C0)}.

% (optional) maximal distances between seeds of the same colour
maxDist2(Max2) :- Max2 = #max{R1,R2,C1,C2 : input(R1,C1,2), input(R2,C2,2), abs(R1 - R2) + abs(C1 - C2)}.
maxDist3(Max3) :- Max3 = #max{R1,R2,C1,C2 : input(R1,C1,3), input(R2,C2,3), abs(R1 - R2) + abs(C1 - C2)}.

% Bounding positions for colour 2
Rmin2 := #min{R : input(R, _, 2)}.
maxCol2 := #max{C : input(_, C, 2)}.

% Bounding positions for colour 3
maxCol3 := #max{C : input(_, C, 3)}.
minCol3 := #min{C : input(_, C, 3)}.

% Start rows for the two vertical legs of colour 3
startRowMaxCol3(Rmax) :- Rmax = #min{R0 : input(R0, maxCol3, 3)}.
startRowMinCol3(Rmax2) :- Rmax2 = #min{R0 : input(R0, minCol3, 3)}.

% Output assignment

output(R,C,2) :- 
    output_cell(R,C), 
    dist2(R,C,D2), dist3(R,C,D3), 
    D2 < D3, 
    R >= Rmin2, 
    C <= maxCol2.

output(R,C,3) :- 
    output_cell(R,C), 
    input(R,C,3).   % cells that are 3 in the input stay 3

output(R,C,3) :- 
    output_cell(R,C), 
    dist3(R,C,D3), dist2(R,C,D2), 
    D3 <= D2, 
    C = maxCol3, 
    R >= startRowMaxCol3(Rmax).

output(R,C,3) :- 
    output_cell(R,C), 
    dist3(R,C,D3), dist2(R,C,D2), 
    D3 <= D2, 
    C = minCol3, 
    R >= startRowMinCol3(Rmax2).

output(R,C,0) :- 
    output_cell(R,C), 
    \+ output(R,C,2), 
    \+ output(R,C,3).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

#show output/3.

% Determine dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% distances to nearest 2 and 3
dist2(R,C,D) :- D = #min{R0,C0 : input(R0,C0,2)} (abs(R - R0) + abs(C - C0)).
dist3(R,C,D) :- D = #min{R0,C0 : input(R0,C0,3)} (abs(R - R0) + abs(C - C0)).

% maximal distances between seeds of the same colour
maxDist2(D) :- D = #max{R1,R2,C1,C2 : input(R1,C1,2), input(R2,C2,2)} (abs(R1 - R2) + abs(C1 - C2)).
maxDist3(D) :- D = #max{R1,R2,C1,C2 : input(R1,C1,3), input(R2,C2,3)} (abs(R1 - R2) + abs(C1 - C2)).

% bounding coordinates for each colour
minRow2(Rmin2) :- Rmin2 = #min{R : input(R, _, 2)}.
maxCol2(Cmax2) :- Cmax2 = #max{C : input(_, C, 2)}.
minRow3(Rmin3) :- Rmin3 = #min{R : input(R, _, 3)}.
minCol3(Cmin3) :- Cmin3 = #min{C : input(_, C, 3)}.

% output colour 3
output(R,C,3) :-
    output_cell(R,C),
    dist3(R,C,D3),
    dist2(R,C,D2),
    D3 <= D2,
    D3 <= MaxDist3,
    R >= Rmin3,
    C >= Cmin3.

% output colour 2
output(R,C,2) :-
    output_cell(R,C),
    dist2(R,C,D2),
    dist3(R,C,D3),
    D2 <= MaxDist2,
    D2 < D3,
    R >= Rmin2,
    C <= Cmax2.

% output colour 0 (default) – allowed only if neither 2 nor 3 can be placed
output(R,C,0) :-
    output_cell(R,C),
    \+ output(R,C,2),
    \+ output(R,C,3).

% Exactly one colour per cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

maxCol2(Cmax2) :- Cmax2 = #max{C : input(_, C, 2)}.
minRow3(Rmin3) :- Rmin3 = #min{R : input(R, _, 3)}.

dist3(R,C,D3) :- D3 = #min{R0,C0 : input(R0,C0,3)} (abs(R - R0) + abs(C - C0)).

maxDist3(M3) :- M3 = #max{R1,R2,C1,C2 : input(R1,C1,3), input(R2,C2,3)} (abs(R1 - R2) + abs(C1 - C2)).
